content: The text provided is a detailed description of various studies, their methodologies, participants, interventions, outcomes, and potential biases. Kim 2015 This study was a retrospective cross-sectional analysis using data from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES V), conducted in South Korea between 2010 and 2012. The study excluded premenopausal women, women without a history of childbirth, and those with secondary causes of osteoporosis, such as rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid disease, or chronic renal failure. The risk of detection bias and reporting bias was deemed unclear. Kim 2020a This prospective cohort study utilized data from the Panel Study on Korean Children (PSKC). Participants were selected through stratified multistage sampling based on resident registration data to represent the nationwide household population. Data were collected through computer-assisted personal interviews. Developmental assessments were conducted using the Korean Ages and Stages Questionnaires (K-ASQ), the Korean version of Denver II, and the Receptive and Expressive Vocabulary Test (REVT). Intelligence and academic performance were evaluated using the Multifactorial Intelligence Test (M-FIT). The risks of selection bias, performance bias, detection bias, and reporting bias were unclear. Kondolot 2017 This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Anthropometry of Turkish Children Aged 0–6 Years (ATCA-06) database, collected between September 2009 and May 2010 in Kayseri, Turkey. A total of 21 Family Health Centers representing various socioeconomic levels were selected. Children were randomly chosen based on family income levels. Exclusion criteria included low birth weight, prematurity, multiple births, chronic or serious diseases, malnutrition, BMI below the 5th percentile, and incomplete records. Parental declarations and medical records were used to complete questionnaires. The risk of reporting bias was unclear. Krenz-Niedbala 2015 This cross-sectional study involved pupils from 31 randomly selected primary schools in Poznań, Poland. Breastfeeding duration was categorized into four groups: less than 3 months, 3–6 months, 7–12 months, and over 12 months. Outcomes included asthma and obesity. The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, exposure classification bias, and other biases were unclear. Kvale 1987 This prospective cohort study invited all women aged 20–69 years in four counties in Norway to participate in a breast cancer screening program between 1956 and 1959. Participants were followed until 1980. Lactation experience for the first three births and total breastfeeding duration were recorded. Outcomes included breast cancer, cervical cancer, carcinoma of the corpus uteri, ovarian cancer, and other cancers. The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, and other biases were unclear. Lee 2003 This prospective cohort study included 129,783 Korean government workers who participated in biennial health maintenance physicals conducted by the Korea Medical Insurance Corporation (KMIC) in 1992. In 1994, 199,521 premenopausal women aged 20 years or older were enrolled in the Korean Women’s Cohort (KWC) Study to assess the effects of gender-related variables on chronic diseases. A total of 110,604 women were followed until December 2000 for breast cancer morbidity and mortality. Exclusion criteria included nulliparity, lack of lactation information, and a prior cancer diagnosis in 1994. Breastfeeding duration was categorized into no lactation, 1–12 months, and 13–24 months. The risk of breast cancer was the primary outcome. The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, and other biases were unclear. Lee 2005 This prospective cohort study analyzed a subsample of individuals insured by KMIC, the largest insurance provider for government employees, teachers, and their families. Premenopausal women aged 20 years or older were included. Exclusion criteria included lack of lactation information and baseline hypertension. Participants were followed for six years. Data collection in 1994 involved a standardized questionnaire on past and present illnesses, menstrual and reproductive factors, and lactation history for up to five children. Breastfeeding duration was calculated as the total lactation duration for all children. The primary outcome was essential hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure ≥140 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg, or current antihypertensive treatment. The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, and other biases were unclear. Lee 2016 This study was part of the MOCEH study, a multicenter prospective birth cohort study. Mothers were asked at 6and 12-month follow-ups about breastfeeding duration and formula use. Participants were categorized into six groups based on breastfeeding duration: formula feeding only, breastfeeding for <3 months, 3–5 months, 6–8 months, 9–11 months, and ≥12 months. Infant development was assessed using the Korean version of the Bayley Scales of Infant Development II at 12, 24, and 36 months. Only Mental Development Index (MDI) scores at 36 months were used for quantitative analyses. The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, and other biases were unclear. Li 2020 This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Zhejiang Aging and Health Cohort Study, which included 5,487 postmenopausal women. Breastfeeding duration was recorded in the reproductive history section of the questionnaire. The mean breastfeeding duration was calculated as the total months of breastfeeding divided by the number of full-term pregnancies. Cognitive impairment was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), with education-specific cut-off scores for cognitive impairment in China. The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, and other biases were unclear. Liese 2001 As part of the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC), two surveys were conducted between September 1995 and December 1996 in Dresden (former East Germany) and Munich (former West Germany). Community-based random samples of children were studied using schools as sampling units. Breastfeeding behavior was assessed with three questions: whether the child was ever breastfed, the duration of breastfeeding, and the duration of exclusive breastfeeding. Outcomes included overweight status, with BMI calculated as weight (kg) divided by height squared (m²). The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, and other biases were unclear. Lima 2019 This prospective cohort study followed women in Pelotas, Brazil, born in 1982, using data from the 1982 Pelotas Birth Cohort Study. All maternity hospitals in Pelotas were visited daily in 1982 to identify all births. Inclusion criteria required at least one live birth, not being pregnant at the time of the interview, and availability of breastfeeding duration and cardiovascular risk factor data. Lifetime breastfeeding duration was calculated by summing the lactation duration for all offspring. Outcomes included systolic and diastolic blood pressure, intima-media thickness, pulse wave velocity, random blood glucose, HDL, LDL, total cholesterol, and non-HDL cholesterol. The risks of confounding bias, selection bias, and other biases were unclear.
